commands.name: capabilities
commands.summary: This document

commands.name: new
commands.summary: Create a named Terminal running a program (resolved on its PATH, never through a shell; or one verbatim command line) in its own pseudo console and job; starts a Host on demand; --profile (or the default profile) starts a shell profile of config.toml

commands.name: ls
commands.summary: Every Terminal of the Host with its state, pid and clients; starts nothing (also `subak list`)

commands.name: info
commands.summary: One Terminal with its window and pane; exit 3 when there is none

commands.name: status
commands.summary: The Host (or that none runs), every Terminal and every client in one answer; starts nothing

commands.name: attach
commands.summary: Interactive attach to a Terminal's pane in this terminal: the screen and history are reproduced, then live output; Ctrl+B d detaches, Ctrl+C goes to the program, nothing is stopped

commands.name: detach
commands.summary: Detach every client of a Terminal, or one client by id; never stops a process

commands.name: rename
commands.summary: Rename a Terminal (unique, case-insensitive); its id never changes

commands.name: stop
commands.summary: End a Terminal's processes (graceful, then forced after 5 s) and keep it as stopped

commands.name: kill
commands.summary: End a Terminal's processes at once and remove the Terminal

commands.name: rm
commands.summary: Remove a Terminal that runs nothing; --force also ends a running one

commands.name: capture
commands.summary: Lines of a pane's screen and history kept by the Host (tmux capture-pane); secret-looking values shown as *** unless --no-redact

commands.name: history
commands.summary: How much of a pane's output the Host keeps (lines, bytes, limits, evictions) and its screen; never the content

commands.name: clear-history
commands.summary: Delete the history the Host keeps for a pane (tmux clear-history); the screen and processes stay

commands.name: host.start
commands.summary: Start a detached per-user Host (one start lock per endpoint), optionally with a first Terminal

commands.name: host.status
commands.summary: Host process id, protocol, job breakaway, environment, idle grace, Terminals and clients

commands.name: host.health
commands.summary: Heartbeat: verify the Host's identity, complete the handshake and measure the answer time

commands.name: host.attach
commands.summary: Interactive attach to the Host's only running pane (as `subak attach` without a target)

commands.name: host.stop
commands.summary: Stop the Host; ending live Terminals needs --kill-terminals and consent

commands.name: host.serve
commands.summary: Run the Host in this process (what host start launches detached)

commands.name: hotkeys.list
commands.summary: The window's shortcuts: every action with its keys, scope, source and state, and the reserved navigation keys

commands.name: hotkeys.show
commands.summary: One shortcut action with its bindings and every conflict that involves it

commands.name: hotkeys.set
commands.summary: Replace an action's bindings in hotkeys.json; a conflicting change is refused (hotkey_conflict) and nothing is written

commands.name: hotkeys.disable
commands.summary: Disable one shortcut, all of them or one scope (e.g. to let programs receive Ctrl+W)

commands.name: hotkeys.enable
commands.summary: Turn all shortcuts or one scope back on

commands.name: hotkeys.reset
commands.summary: Restore an action's default, or discard every change (--all keeps hotkeys.json.bak)

commands.name: hotkeys.check
commands.summary: Conflict report for Subak's shortcuts; --all-tools reads every installed Kim tool's hotkey files (starts nothing)

commands.name: hotkeys.export
commands.summary: Print Subak's hotkeys.json user layer

commands.name: hotkeys.import
commands.summary: Validate a kim.hotkeys document and replace the user layer (keeps a backup)

commands.name: config.show
commands.summary: Every setting of config.toml with its value, default and source, the shell profiles (secret-looking values as ***), problems and unknown keys

commands.name: config.check
commands.summary: Validate config.toml: every problem with its key and line; exits 0 (valid tells)

commands.name: config.set
commands.summary: Change one setting by editing its line in place (comments and unknown keys stay); an invalid value is refused and nothing is written

commands.name: config.reset
commands.summary: Return settings to their defaults; --all keeps a backup and also replaces an invalid file

commands.name: config.export
commands.summary: Print config.toml (or the defaults) with every secret-looking value replaced by ***

commands.name: config.import
commands.summary: Validate a settings file and replace config.toml with it (keeps a backup); secrets are refused (secret_in_config)

commands.name: profile.list
commands.summary: The shell profiles of config.toml, secret-looking values as ***

commands.name: profile.show
commands.summary: One shell profile (names ignore case)

commands.name: window.new
commands.summary: A new internal window (tmux new-window) with one pane running its own process in a running Terminal; it becomes the active one unless --no-select

commands.name: window.ls
commands.summary: The internal windows of a Terminal with their panes and the active window (tmux list-windows)

commands.name: window.select
commands.summary: Make a window the Terminal's active one for every client (tmux select-window); no process changes

commands.name: window.rename
commands.summary: Rename an internal window (names need not be unique; not only digits)

commands.name: window.kill
commands.summary: End the processes of one window's panes at once and remove the window; every other pane keeps running; the last window is refused (use kill)

commands.name: pane.new
commands.summary: A new pane with its own process in a window: a vertical split of the window's active pane (see pane.split)
commands.usage: subak pane new <terminal | terminal:window | w-id> [--no-select] [--cwd <dir>] [--env NAME[=VALUE]]... [--unset-env NAME]... [--size <cols>x<rows>] [--history-limit <lines>] [--command-line <line> | -- <program> [args...]] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: pane.ls
commands.summary: The panes of a Terminal or of one window, with pids, programs and the active ones (tmux list-panes)

commands.name: pane.select
commands.summary: Make a pane (or its neighbour in a direction) its window's active one and that window the Terminal's (tmux select-pane); no process changes
commands.usage: subak pane select <terminal:window.pane | p-id> [left | right | up | down | next | previous] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: pane.kill
commands.summary: End one pane's processes at once and remove it; every other pane keeps running; the last pane is refused (use kill)

commands.name: pane.split
commands.summary: Split a pane and start a new pane with its own process next to it, stacked (default) or side by side (tmux split-window); the panes share the window's size
commands.usage: subak pane split <terminal | terminal:window | terminal:window.pane | p-id> [--horizontal | --vertical] [--before] [--cells <n> | --percent <n>] [--no-select] [--cwd <dir>] [--env NAME[=VALUE]]... [--unset-env NAME]... [--history-limit <lines>] [--command-line <line> | -- <program> [args...]] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: pane.resize
commands.summary: Move a pane's border (tmux resize-pane -L/-R/-U/-D); the panes are resized, every process keeps running
commands.usage: subak pane resize <terminal:window.pane | p-id> <left | right | up | down> [cells] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: pane.swap
commands.summary: Swap two panes of a window (tmux swap-pane); processes stay with their panes
commands.usage: subak pane swap <terminal:window.pane | p-id> <other pane | next | previous> [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: pane.zoom
commands.summary: Let a pane fill its window, or give it its place back (tmux resize-pane -Z); a toggle by default

commands.name: window.rotate
commands.summary: Move every pane of a window one place (tmux rotate-window); processes stay with their panes
commands.usage: subak window rotate <terminal | terminal:window | w-id> [up | down] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: window.layout
commands.summary: Arrange a window's panes with a tmux layout preset, the next or previous one, or spread them evenly (tmux select-layout, next-layout, select-layout -E)
commands.usage: subak window layout <terminal | terminal:window | w-id> <even-horizontal | even-vertical | main-horizontal[-mirrored] | main-vertical[-mirrored] | tiled | next | previous | spread> [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: command
commands.summary: Run tmux command lines (split-window, select-pane, send-keys, break-pane, join-pane, set-buffer, list-panes, setw, set-hook, display-message -p, last-window, …) on a Terminal; kill-* need --yes
commands.usage: subak command [--target <target>] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] '<tmux command>[; <tmux command>]…' (also `subak tmux`, or the words after --)

commands.name: buffer.ls
commands.summary: The Host's paste buffers (tmux list-buffers): names, sizes and a redacted first line

commands.name: buffer.show
commands.summary: One paste buffer's text, the newest without a name (tmux show-buffer)

commands.name: buffer.set
commands.summary: Put text in a paste buffer of the Host (tmux set-buffer); memory only, never written

commands.name: buffer.delete
commands.summary: Delete a paste buffer, the newest without a name (tmux delete-buffer)

commands.name: buffer.paste
commands.summary: Type a paste buffer into a pane as input (tmux paste-buffer)

commands.name: claude.hooks.status
commands.summary: Whether Subak's Claude Code hooks are in a settings file (default ~/.claude/settings.json); other hooks are counted, never changed

commands.name: claude.hooks.install
commands.summary: Opt in: merge Subak's hook entries into a Claude Code settings file, keeping every other setting and hook; a backup first

commands.name: claude.hooks.uninstall
commands.summary: Remove exactly Subak's hook entries from a Claude Code settings file; a backup first

commands.name: claude.report
commands.summary: Run by a Claude Code hook: forward the event and session id (nothing else) to the pane's Host; prints nothing, always exits 0

commands.name: claude.status
commands.summary: The Claude Code sessions per pane that hooks reported (states idle, in-progress, need-input, done, unknown)

commands.name: state.show
commands.summary: The saved Terminal topology in state.json (read only; nothing is started or changed)

commands.name: state.check
commands.summary: Verify state.json: schema, CRC, structure; reports missing working directories and programs

commands.name: state.backups
commands.summary: The state backups (newest 5) and whether each is valid

commands.name: state.forget
commands.summary: Remove a saved Terminal record (through the running Host, else in the file after a backup)

commands.name: state.policy
commands.summary: Whether a Terminal is restored when Subak next opens; starts and ends nothing

commands.name: state.rollback
commands.summary: Make a backup (default: the newest valid one) the current state; refused while a Host runs

commands.name: recover.list
commands.summary: The saved Terminals the Host can restore, pane by pane, and what a restore cannot bring back (starts nothing)

commands.name: recover
commands.summary: Start a saved Terminal again: its id, name, windows and layout with fresh shells; the saved Claude session or start commands only when asked

commands.name: shell-integration.status
commands.summary: Whether the optional shell integration (the shell reports its folder) is in the PowerShell profile; for cmd, the per-profile opt-in

commands.name: shell-integration.install
commands.summary: Opt in: add Subak's marked block to the PowerShell profile (a backup first; active only in Subak panes)

commands.name: shell-integration.uninstall
commands.summary: Remove exactly Subak's block from the PowerShell profile (a backup first)

commands.name: ssh.connect
commands.summary: A Terminal whose pane runs Windows' OpenSSH client: strict host-key checking (the user answers a new host), jump hosts, loopback port forwards, agent and X11 forwarding only when asked (with a warning), a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, an auditable login script, a saved secret only for a verified host
commands.usage: subak ssh connect <[user@]host[:port]> [<name>] [--identity <key>] [--option Key=Value]... [--ssh-config <file>] [--jump <[user@]host[:port]>]... [--forward L:[bind:]port:host:port|R:[bind:]port:host:port|D:[bind:]port]... [--allow-public-bind] [--no-shell] [--agent-forward] [--x11] [--proxy socks5://host:port|http://host:port] [--login-script <file>] [--env NAME[=VALUE]]... [--cwd <dir>] [--attach] [--no-start] [--dry-run] [--endpoint <name>] [--json]

commands.name: ssh.credential.status
commands.summary: Whether a password or passphrase is saved in Windows Credential Manager and whether the host is in known_hosts (never the secret)

commands.name: ssh.credential.save
commands.summary: Save a password or key passphrase in Windows Credential Manager, for a host already in known_hosts; read without echo or from one stdin line, never printed

commands.name: ssh.credential.forget
commands.summary: Remove the saved secret of a destination from Windows Credential Manager

commands.name: sftp.ls
commands.summary: List a remote directory over SFTP (the host must be in known_hosts; never a prompt)

commands.name: sftp.get
commands.summary: Download a file or folder: a *.subak-part file renamed when complete, existing files kept unless --overwrite, unsafe remote names refused, links never followed
commands.usage: subak sftp get <[user@]host[:port]> <remote path> [<local path>] [--identity <key>] [--option Key=Value]... [--ssh-config <file>] [--jump <[user@]host[:port]>]... [--proxy <url>] [--recursive] [--overwrite|--resume] [--background] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: sftp.put
commands.summary: Upload a file or folder (0644/0755, --private 0600/0700) through a *.subak-part file; existing files kept unless --overwrite
commands.usage: subak sftp put <[user@]host[:port]> <local path> [<remote path>] [--identity <key>] [--option Key=Value]... [--ssh-config <file>] [--jump <[user@]host[:port]>]... [--proxy <url>] [--recursive] [--overwrite|--resume] [--private] [--background] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: sftp.mkdir
commands.summary: Create a remote directory

commands.name: sftp.rm
commands.summary: Delete a remote file or empty directory (needs --yes)

commands.name: transfer.list
commands.summary: Background transfers and their state and progress (never a secret)

commands.name: transfer.status
commands.summary: One background transfer: state, bytes and files done, its error

commands.name: transfer.cancel
commands.summary: Stop a background transfer between chunks; the partial file is kept for --resume

commands.name: telnet.connect
commands.summary: A Terminal running Subak's Telnet bridge; off by default (needs --allow-insecure) and always warned about because it is unencrypted

commands.name: serial.list
commands.summary: The serial ports Windows lists (read only)

commands.name: serial.connect
commands.summary: A Terminal running Subak's serial bridge on a COM port with the line settings given
commands.usage: subak serial connect <COMn> [<name>] [--baud <n>] [--data-bits 5-8] [--parity none|odd|even|mark|space] [--stop-bits 1|1.5|2] [--flow none|rtscts|xonxoff] [--newline cr|lf|crlf] [--local-echo] [--attach] [--no-start] [--dry-run] [--endpoint <name>] [--json]

commands.name: ssh.hosts
commands.summary: The Host entries of ~/.ssh/config (HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile, ProxyJump), read only

commands.name: mcp.serve
commands.summary: A Model Context Protocol server on stdin/stdout for the agent that starts it: read-only (redacted screens) unless the user grants more; no network listener

commands.name: mcp.tools
commands.summary: The MCP tools a server with these grants offers, with schemas and annotations

commands.name: interop.invoke
commands.summary: Run one Kim interop capability (terminal.list, terminal.open, terminal.paste-path) from a request on stdin; dry runs change nothing

commands.name: host.stats
commands.summary: The running Host's memory, handles, CPU time and counters (sessions, IPC, scrollback); starts nothing

provides.summary: The Terminals of the user's Subak Host (id, name, state); starts nothing
Open a new Terminal with the default shell or a profile (params: name, cwd, profile)
Type an existing file's quoted path into a pane, without Enter (params: target, path)

data.summary: Pre-alpha: per-user Host with IPC v1, named Terminals (new, ls, attach, rename, kill, capture…), windows and panes, subak-gui tabs, hotkeys, settings and profiles; no split layouts or recovery yet
